newsitem.title: CHINA: China play on HK stresses strength of Chinese race.
newsitem.headline: China play on HK stresses strength of Chinese race.

text.p: China must be strong and Chinese people must have a strong sense of their unique spirit to survive -- that is the lesson of Hong Kong, says the director of a new Shanghai play on the colony.

The play, called "Gui Lai Xi" (Please Return), is due to open in Beijing on Saturday night, two days before the British hand Hong Kong back to China after 156 years of colonial rule. "The message is that everyone should have a sense of responsibility towards the Chinese race," said director Lu Ang.
"The race must be strong before we as individuals can be safe and stable. Chinese people mustn't forget the Chinese spirit," he said.

The play will be performed in Beijing through to July 3, replacing a production by the People's Liberation Army which in Lu Ang's phrase had been "executed" by the authorities for reasons that are not clear.
"Gui Lai Xi" will then come home to Shanghai for another five performances.
The play follows the life of a Shanghai businessman who in his youth is encouraged by the founder of modern China, Sun Yat-sen, to think not only of money but also of the fate of the nation.
The businessman moves the machinery in his factory to Hong Kong when the Japanese take over Shanghai in the late 1930s, and his wife commits suicide rather than betray him to the invading forces.
In the 1960s, the businessman is in Hong Kong when the colony is saved from a disastrous drought when a benevolent China turns on the water taps.
The highlight of the show is a scene in which late Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping and former British prime minister Margaret Thatcher discuss the return of Hong Kong.
"This is the first time for an old Deng Xiaoping to be depicted in a play," said Lu. "It couldn't be done while he was alive."
The reaction from audiences in test performances so far had been good, Lu said.
"People expect there to be a very heavy propaganda element to the play, but there isn't. We've tried to make it as much of a work of art as possible," he said.
